item.title: Re: Author post
item.content:encoded:
My thoughts and motivations:

I strongly dislike utilitarian ethics, though it’s a pretty popular system among a lot of my friends. I don’t believe that there’s a spectrum of positive to negative utility, and I don’t believe that good cancels out evil. If you’ve used evil to accomplish something good, that doesn’t mean the evil doesn’t count. You’ve just done both.

Zeta Zero exists because there’s no such thing as the lesser evil, there’s just the preferable evil. If the Foundation sees that there’s a choice between killing one child or allowing dozens of bystanders to die, they’ll choose the former, but that doesn’t make it “good,” or even less evil. It’s just the evil that was their best option.

Members of Zeta Zero know that they are not fighting for the greater good. Anybody who can absolve themselves of guilt by committing atrocities in the name of the greater good is dangerous, and can’t be trusted to show good judgement. If you’re convinced of your own righteousness, there’s very little to stop you.

People join Zeta Zero because their reconditioning program can ease the pain of their past actions, and allow them to function. Anybody who volunteers out of a desire to kill for the greater good is rejected. They only take people who fully understand that their actions are evil, and then reshape their minds to allow them to do that dispassionately.

A fully reconditioned Zeta Zero has a lot of operational discretion in the field. They never shoot first and ask questions later. They understand that their targets might be effectively innocent, and should not be harmed without reason. The Foundation has figured out the trick of rebuilding people to still have a conscience, but be able to violate it without hesitation if need be. Zero-sum situations where killing a child is the only solution are very, very rare. Most Zeta Zero missions end without firing a shot, but they can be trusted to do so if necessary.

It’s not the moral security of the greater good, it’s the ability to choose to do evil. None of them want to be a Monster, but they’ll do it anyway.

item.content:encoded:
This…this is something I both hate and like. It is very true. Heck, my brother is a veteran of Iraq, drive a transport, and he barely talks about it but once mentioned that he was told to either run over or shoot a kid who attempted to stop the convoy…IRL terrorists use children as weapons through indoctrination. Anomalous diseases, curses, they don't choose targets. Rheumatological malignant entities act through what is available. hell, some kind of An-Terror group might actively use children.

I don't really see this as grim-dark. Zeta-0 clearly do not enjoy their job, which is good. WOnder how many use amnestics constantly, and how many live with the scars of what they ahve seen and done so as to remember everything they are trying to prevent. When it comes to cold numbers, 1 child or teen, vs hundreds, well, you gotta do what must be done, even if you hate yourself for it.

item.title: Author post
item.content:encoded:
I don't normally write violent or grimdark fiction, but I had the idea for an atrocity Mobile Task Force, and wanted to see what happened if I wrote it. Thanks to Zyn for feedback on the forums, and several others on IRC (chime in if I left you out!)

For more of my stuff, a lot of which is significantly more lighthearted, check out my Author Page. I particularly recommend SCP-4357 if you're looking for something funny.
